folder_html:
LIVE WATER CLARITY / TURBIDITY

Diffuse attenuation coefficient for photosynthetically available radiation (KdPAR): how quickly sunlight fades with depth. Larger values mean more turbid water; smaller values mean clearer water. Source values are never altered for color convenience.

Diffuse attenuation coefficient for PAR (m^-1), FIXED log-spaced scale LOWEST 0.02 clearest (dark blue) → 0.1 → 0.3 → 1.0 turbid (red) → HIGHEST+ 5+ most turbid (violet). Larger values always mean murkier water; source values are never altered.

Exact variable: kd_par (Diffuse Attenuation Coefficient for PAR; NOAA MECB algorithm; product status Experimental)
Units: m^-1
Source: NOAA CoastWatch S-NPP VIIRS Kd(PAR) diffuse attenuation, Global 4 km, Daily (ERDDAP; newest-wins across nesdisVHNkdparDaily NRT and nesdisVHNSQkdparDaily Science Quality, per-day fallback) + MODIS Aqua Kd490 NRT (erdMH1kd4901day_R2022NRT) daily fallback for days KdPAR lacks
Update: daily composites
Data time: 2026-09-29 08:00 AM EDT (mosaic 2026-09-29..2026-09-23)
Processed: 2026-10-02 11:41 PM EDT
Why turbid water turns red/purple: Rare very-turbid water (storm resuspension, river plumes, intense blooms) compresses into red-violet/deep-purple; ordinary clear conditions own most of the color resolution.
Provenance: ERDDAP dataset
